meta.name: Building Layout wizard commands
meta.recommended_approach: One LLM call per user turn with tool/function calling (temperature 0), using llm_tools below. The LLM extracts the intent and raw slots and nothing else. App code resolves references, normalizes units (parseFtIn), builds ops, runs every validation deterministically on a structuredClone of the model after regenerate(), shows a preview with the takeoff delta, and applies with an undo snapshot. Never let the LLM write the model or produce code facts, prices or sizes.
meta.money: All $ are EXAMPLE from content-v3/homedepot-prices.json (homedepot.com default online store snapshot 2026-10-28, not Denver). No invented prices.

conventions.coords: plan ft; x -> east, y -> south (js/geom.js). footprint = outside face of framing.

directions.right: east (plan view; in 3D resolve from the camera)
directions.left: west (plan view; in 3D resolve from the camera)

conventions.opening_left_right: as seen from outside the wall
conventions.height: plate height = top of top plate above the subfloor (walls.params.plateHeightFt). 'above ground' adds walls.zBase.
conventions.shed_run: distance between outside faces of the high and low walls (footprint dimension); centerline value shown as a footnote

units.bare_number: ft for lengths/heights >= 4, in for opening sizes; otherwise ask

conventions.wall_resolution: exterior wall side from the outward normal of footprint edge i (wall id w-ext-i); ties -> ask; 'this' -> m.selection; 'house side' -> m.attachToExistingWallId or the existing site object touching the footprint

proposed_fields.m.wizard.log: optional chat log; undo stack NOT persisted in the model

args: offsetFt (+ = inward, same math as edit-ops applyDrag 'edge')

intents.description: Change the roof to a single-slope (shed) roof using a high and low wall height, or a pitch.
examples: put the roof higher at one end so it goes from 10ft to 8feet
make it a shed roof, 10 ft at the house and 8 ft at the far wall
slope the roof from the back down to the front
single slope roof 1.5 in 12 sloping south

highHeight.description: Length exactly as the user said it, e.g. '10ft', "8' 6\"", '102 in'. App code normalizes with parseFtIn().

lowHeight.description: Length exactly as the user said it, e.g. '10ft', "8' 6\"", '102 in'. App code normalizes with parseFtIn().

highSide.description: How the user referred to the wall: compass ('north'), position ('back','front','left','right'), 'this' (selection), 'the long wall', 'the house side', 'wall with the door'. App code resolves it to a wall id.

clarify_when: highSide missing or 'one end'/'one side' → chips for each exterior wall side with the resulting pitch; if attachToExistingWallId or an existing building touches a wall, ask to confirm high side = house side (slope away from the house)
heightMeaning unclear ('10 ft off the ground', 'roof height') → ask wall height vs above ground
non-rectangular footprint → ask which wall is high and warn that the v1 shed is drawn over the bounding rectangle
intents.notes: Pitch = (highPlateFt - lowPlateFt) / run * 12, run = footprint distance between the outside faces of the high and low walls. Low wall = the exterior wall parallel and opposite to the high wall. The side walls become rake walls. Requires shed generation (status: needs_app_support until App Builder adds shedGeometry).

validations.rule: Every pier center (auto or manual) within PIERS.offWallTolFt (0.5 ft) of a bearing line (exterior or interior bearing:true wall centerline). No mid-span piers. Grade beam on those lines.
validations.message: Piers only go under walls and at corners, never mid-span, with a grade beam on those lines. Try deeper joists that clear-span, or make that a bearing wall.

validations.rule: After a footprint/wall change, manual piers with props.flags (off wall line / outside footprint) are listed.
validations.message: {n} pier(s) are no longer under a wall. They were kept. Move them back under the walls or reset to auto?
The floor spans {span}, so a mid beam is added and FLAGGED (not sized, no supports). Under the piers-under-walls rule, deeper joists (e.g. 2x12, verify span table) are usually better.
Frost depth isn't entered, so footings and piers are drawn at a 24 in placeholder. Ask your building department.
Expansive soil: you'll likely need a soils report and engineered piers.
The grade beam bottom is {x} in above ground. That needs supported forms. Ask about casting it at grade.
{covering} needs at least {min}:12 (IRC {section}). This roof would be {pitch}:12.
Between 2:12 and 4:12, asphalt shingles need two layers of underlayment (IRC R905.2.2, Table R905.1.1(2)).
Check your panel's minimum slope. The manufacturer can be stricter than code.
Low-slope roof: make sure the low edge drains away from the house and walkways (IRC R903.4). Snow sits longer, so follow the roofing maker's underlayment/ice-barrier instructions.

validations.rule: any change to roof span, pitch, shape, rafterSize or rafterOcIn
validations.message: Rafters span about {span} (horizontal). Check {rafterSize} @ {oc} in against the IRC rafter span tables for your snow load (R802.4.1), or ask your engineer.

validations.rule: rafterLen + 0.5 ft > max stock length priced (20 ft)
validations.message: {len} rafters are longer than any board in the price list and can't be spliced mid-span without support.
Ridge, ridge cap, collar ties and gable framing removed. Ceiling joists are typically not needed as rafter ties when rafters bear on walls at both ends. Verify.
Hip roofs aren't generated yet.
Shed roofs aren't drawn yet in this version. Here are the numbers; nothing was changed.
source: js/generate.js: 'Only gable is generated in v1; shed and hip are coming.'

validations.rule: stud length (plateFt*12 - 1.5*(bottomPlates+topPlates)) > 120 in for any wall (incl. the rake-wall high end)
validations.message: Studs over 10 ft need extra lateral support or design (IRC Table R602.3(5)).

validations.rule: opening.widthIn > 72 → header '2-2x12 (verify — long span)'; always EXAMPLE header
validations.message: Header {header} is from an EXAMPLE table. Verify. Openings over 6 ft usually need an engineered header. In 2x6 walls add a 3rd ply or filler.

validations.rule: opening fits wall (width + 2*(jack+king) <= len - 0.6 ft), no overlap with other openings' rough openings+king/jack, sillIn + heightIn + header depth + plates <= plate height at t
validations.message: That doesn't fit: {why}.

validations.rule: opening edge within 24 in of a corner
validations.message: This opening is close to the corner, which leaves less wall for bracing. Verify with your building department.
source: general practice (not a cited code value)

validations.message: {n} opening(s) on that wall will be removed.

validations.rule: interior wall endpoints inside the footprint, length >= 2 ft
validations.message: That wall would be outside the building or too short.
Exterior walls come from the footprint. Move or resize the footprint instead.

validations.rule: regenerate flag 'Footprint crosses a setback line.'
validations.message: The building now crosses a setback line.

validations.message: Building against the house (ledger, flashing, tying in) is a permit and engineer trigger.
{item} needs a price. It isn't in the Home Depot snapshot, so the total isn't complete.
EXAMPLE, homedepot.com online snapshot {snapshot_date}, not a Denver store; 'est.' for verified:false.

code_facts.note: Model IRC text read on UpCodes (2021 IRC as adopted in the 2022 CT code, and 2024 IRC/GSA). codes.iccsafe.org returned 403 to this fetch. Local adopted edition and amendments govern.

asphalt_shingle.extra: 2:12 to <4:12: double underlayment per R905.1.1 / Table R905.1.1(2)

metal_panel_lapped.extra: lapped, nonsoldered seams, no applied lap sealant

studHeight.fact: Bearing 2x4/2x6 studs: 10 ft laterally unsupported height (Table R602.3(5)); exceptions in R602.3.1

rafterSpan.fact: Rafter spans per Tables R802.4.1(1)-(8), measured on the horizontal projection (R802.4.1). Not tabulated in this content; the wizard warns only.

rafterTies.fact: Rafters meeting at a ridge need ceiling joists/rafter ties as continuous ties (R802.5.2) or a designed ridge beam (R802.3).

drainage.fact: Unless roofs are sloped to drain over roof edges, roof drains are required at each low point (R903.4).

iceBarrier.fact: Ice barrier required for listed coverings where the jurisdiction designates a history of ice damming (R905.1.2, Table R301.2).
